    Fitting the SDT model

    sdt_fitting.Rd

    Fitting the SDT model. NB: Best results are obtained with the "DEoptim" method and at least 1e4 trials.

    sdt_fitting(
  data,
  method = c("expectation", "simulation"),
  ntrials = 10000,
  log_mse = TRUE,
  loss = c("multinomial", "mse"),
  fit_method = c("DEoptim", "nlminb", "Nelder-Mead", "CG", "BFGS", "L-BFGS-B", "bobyqa",
    "grid"),
  cluster = NULL,
  grid_res = 0.05,
  maxit = 100,
  internal_noise_upper_bound = 10,
  confint = TRUE,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  confint_grid_length = 501,
  return_profiles = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  return_grid = FALSE,
  smooth_grid = TRUE,
  plot_surface = TRUE,
  fine_res = 200,
  smooth_k = 20,
  response_levels = NULL
)

    Arguments

    data

    Dataframe, with observed prop_agree and prop_int1.

    method

    Character, the method for computing prop_agree and prop_first ("simulation" or "expectation").

    ntrials

    Numeric, number of simulated trials in the SDT model.

    log_mse

    Logical, should we return the log-MSE (instead of the MSE).

    loss

    Character. Loss function to minimise. Either "mse" for the original mean squared error on summary proportions, or "multinomial" for the multinomial negative log-likelihood on full double-pass response patterns.

    fit_method

    Character, the optimisation method, see possible values below (DEoptim seems to work best). Beware that method "grid" can take some time, depending on the size of the grid.

    cluster

    Character, existing parallel cluster object. If provided, overrides + specified parallelType.

    grid_res

    Numeric, grid resolution in units of response bias or internal noise (only used for method "grid").

    maxit

    Numeric, maximum number of iterations.

    internal_noise_upper_bound

    Numeric, upper bound for internal noise estimation.

    confint

    Logical, whether to compute profile-likelihood confidence intervals for response bias and internal noise. Only available when loss = "multinomial".

    conf_level

    Numeric, confidence level for profile-likelihood confidence intervals.

    confint_grid_length

    Numeric, number of grid points used for each one-dimensional profile likelihood.

    return_profiles

    Logical, whether to return the full profile-likelihood objects in addition to the confidence interval table.

    verbose

    Logical, whether to print progress during fitting.

    return_grid

    Logical, should we return the full grid when method = "grid".

    smooth_grid

    Logical, should we smooth the error surface (grid) with a GAM.

    plot_surface

    Logical, should we plot the GAM-smoothed error surface.

    fine_res

    Numeric, finer grid resolution for plotting the GAM-smoothed error surface.

    smooth_k

    Numeric, k value in mgcv::gam() for smoothing the error surface.

    response_levels

    Optional length-2 vector specifying the observed response labels corresponding to stim1 and stim2. The first value is mapped to stim1, and the second value is mapped to stim2. For example, use response_levels = c(0, 1) when 0 means stim1 and 1 means stim2.

    Value

    The optimised parameter values and further convergence information. If confint = TRUE, the returned object also contains profile-likelihood confidence intervals.

    Author

    Ladislas Nalborczyk ladislas.nalborczyk@cnrs.fr.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Generate full double-pass data for multinomial fitting
sdt_df <- sdt_data(
    pars = c(1, 2),
    method = "simulation",
    ntrials = 200,
    return_summary = FALSE
    )

# Fit with the multinomial likelihood using DEoptim
sdt_fit <- sdt_fitting(
    data = sdt_df,
    method = "expectation",
    loss = "multinomial",
    fit_method = "DEoptim",
    ntrials = nrow(sdt_df),
    maxit = 200,
    internal_noise_upper_bound = 10,
    confint = TRUE
    )

# Point estimates and profile-likelihood confidence intervals
sdt_fit$confint

# MSE fitting on summary proportions
sdt_summary <- sdt_data(pars = c(1, 2), ntrials = 200)

sdt_summary_fit <- sdt_fitting(
    data = sdt_summary,
    method = "expectation",
    loss = "mse",
    fit_method = "DEoptim",
    ntrials = 1000,
    maxit = 200
    )

# Point estimates
sdt_summary_fit$optim$bestmem
} # }
